headline: Police use sound grenades to disperse garment workers in Gazipur
summary: Workers from C Stage BD Limited blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway to demand unpaid September wages after factory owners failed to meet a payment deadline.
details: Police deployed sound grenades to disperse garment factory workers who blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Gazipur's Sreepur on Thursday morning.
The protesters, employees of C Stage BD Limited, took positions in the MC Bazar area of Mulaid village around 8:30 am, causing long tailbacks in both directions.
Workers stated they had previously demonstrated on October 10 over unpaid September wages and were promised payment by October 13, but the factory authorities failed to deliver.
Gazipur Industrial Police-2 Superintendent Mohammad Amjad Hossain stated that officers first asked the protesters to clear the road and offered to discuss demands with owners.
When the workers refused to leave the highway, police used several sound grenades to clear the road and restore traffic flow within about an hour.
Superintendent Amjad added that a final decision on the outstanding wages will be made following further discussions with the factory owners.
caption:

headline_marked: Former BCL leader [[Siam jailed for 4 years]] in graft case
headline: Former BCL leader Siam jailed for 4 years in graft case
summary: Syed Sohanur Rahman Siam was convicted of acquiring wealth beyond his known sources of income, with the court ordering the confiscation of Tk 3.18 million.
details: A Dhaka court has sentenced Syed Sohanur Rahman Siam, a former leader of the now-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL), to four years in prison for acquiring wealth beyond his known sources of income.
Dhaka Divisional Special Judge BM Tariqul Kabir delivered the verdict on Thursday. Siam was also fined Tk 20,000, with an additional six months of rigorous imprisonment if he fails to pay.
The court ordered the confiscation of Tk 3.18 million in illegally acquired assets in favor of the state.
Siam is the son of Syed Abed Ali Jibon, a former driver for a Public Service Commission (PSC) chairman who was involved in the PSC question paper leak scandal.
Siam previously served as the relief and disaster management secretary of Dhaka Metropolitan North Chhatra League but was removed from his post in July 2024 over alleged involvement in the leak.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on January 5, 2025, accusing Siam of acquiring Tk 3.73 million in illegal wealth between September 2021 and June 2024.
The investigation identified movable and immovable assets worth Tk 3.18 million that were inconsistent with his known sources of income.
During the trial, the court heard testimony from 11 witnesses and closing arguments from both the prosecution and defense before delivering the verdict.
caption:
A former BCL leader has been sentenced to 4 years in prison for illegal wealth. The court also ordered the confiscation of millions in assets.

A Dhaka court has sentenced Syed Sohanur Rahman Siam, a former leader of the now-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL), to four years in prison for acquiring wealth beyond his known sources of income.

Dhaka Divisional Special Judge BM Tariqul Kabir delivered the verdict on Thursday. Siam was also fined Tk 20,000, with an additional six months of rigorous imprisonment if he fails to pay.

The court ordered the confiscation of Tk 3.18 million in illegally acquired assets in favor of the state.

Siam is the son of Syed Abed Ali Jibon, a former driver for a Public Service Commission (PSC) chairman who was involved in the PSC question paper leak scandal.

Siam previously served as the relief and disaster management secretary of Dhaka Metropolitan North Chhatra League but was removed from his post in July 2024 over alleged involvement in the leak.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on January 5, 2025, accusing Siam of acquiring Tk 3.73 million in illegal wealth between September 2021 and June 2024.

The investigation identified movable and immovable assets worth Tk 3.18 million that were inconsistent with his known sources of income.

During the trial, the court heard testimony from 11 witnesses and closing arguments from both the prosecution and defense before delivering the verdict.
